subject: Basic GGIR Question: Processing Data from Wrist Worn Accelerometer

messages.author: 8b544cbd8df3ddb3
messages.subject: Basic GGIR Question: Processing Data from Wrist Worn Accelerometer
parts:
Hello all,

      Firstly, thanks again for creation of the GGIR package. 

      I'm a GGIR beginner, and have been tasked with trying to find out how to process data from wrist worn ActiGraph wGT3X-BT accelerometers that we're using with adults.

      Would it be sufficient for us to just use the default GGIR settings, and specify the "Hildebrand et al 2014/2016" settings in section 2.3.4 of the GGIR CRAN vignette? By "sufficient", I mean acceptable by publication reviewers and/or accelerometry experts (which then implies "correctness"). 

       Thanks in advance!
        Raymond

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Basic GGIR Question: Processing Data from Wrist Worn Accelerometer
parts:
Hi Raymond,

Good question. GGIR's default arguments values are set to be reasonable for wrist-accelerometer data.  A number of argument values are study design specific and by that need to be set on a per-study basis, e.g. how much time to exclude at start and end of recording, or in relation to the sleeplog.

GGIR is open-source, which means that it comes without any warranties. It is your responsibility to make sure you use it correctly and to remain critical at all times. Only with a critical user community we can make sure that GGIR keeps improving.

Best wishes,
Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
